summary: Verified fix: redact_json_value now threads the parent key into list items (redact_json_value(item, key=key) for item in value), so a list of plain strings under a secret-shaped key (e.g. "tokens": ["abc123...", ...]) is now redacted where it previously was not. Empirically confirmed against the live implementation with a synthetic sample. Scanned all 2080 JSON files under the tool's actual candidate scan roots (docs/03-reference/dcp, contracts/openclaw-dcp-routing, schemas/dcp*, src/dopemux/dcp, services/dcp-readonly-facade, tests/dcp*, task-packets/dcp, proof/) for the one remaining structural gap in the fix (list-of-dicts nested under a secret-shaped key, where the dict's own keys override and discard the parent's key context) — zero real occurrences found, so the gap is real but currently dormant in this corpus. No automated test file exists for this script (tools/dcp/build_comprehensive_bundle.py has no counterpart under tests/).

findings.title: Key context is lost when a list under a secret-shaped key contains dicts
findings.body: redact_json_value only forwards parent `key` to list *items*; when an item is itself a dict, the recursive dict branch immediately overwrites `key` with the dict's own keys (redact_json_value(item, key=str(k)) for k,item in value.items()). So e.g. {"secrets": [{"value": "<realsecret>"}]} would NOT be redacted, because once inside the dict, only "value" is checked against _SECRET_JSON_KEY, not "secrets". Confirmed via direct execution of the current redact_json_value against a synthetic sample. However, a scan of all 2080 JSON files under the tool's actual scan roots (docs/03-reference/dcp, contracts/openclaw-dcp-routing, schemas/dcp*, src/dopemux/dcp, services/dcp-readonly-facade, tests/dcp*, task-packets/dcp, proof/) found zero instances of this shape today, so it is a latent gap, not an active leak in this bundle's current inputs.

findings.title: Key-based redaction threshold silently exempts short values
findings.body: The `len(value) > 8` guard in redact_json_value means a field like {"token": "abcd"} is left untouched even though the key is secret-shaped. Low real-world impact (short strings are unlikely to be live credentials) but is an unremarked edge in the redaction contract.

findings.title: No automated regression test for the bundle generator or its redaction behavior
findings.body: tools/dcp/build_comprehensive_bundle.py has no corresponding test file (checked tests/dcp, tests/dcp_extension, tests/unit/dcp). The list-redaction fix that prompted this re-audit was verified only by manual/ad hoc execution here, not by CI-enforced tests, so a future refactor could silently regress it.

remaining_risks: Regex-based secret detection (REDACTIONS list) is inherently incomplete for credential shapes not matching its patterns.
Non-text-extension files are copied via shutil.copy2 with no content scanning at all.
List-of-dicts nested under a secret-shaped key bypasses key-based redaction (F1) — dormant today, not structurally prevented.
Key names themselves are never redacted, only values.
